issues.title: Direct import from features package
issues.description: The rule requires apps/api/v2 to import from @calcom/platform-libraries instead of directly from @calcom/features, but the code imports TeamService directly from @calcom/features/ee/teams/services/teamService
issues.rule_name: Prevent Circular Dependencies Between Core Packages

issues.title: Insufficient authorization - regular members can create invite links
issues.description: The endpoint uses @Roles('TEAM_MEMBER') which allows any team member to create invite links, but the business logic requires admin permissions for this sensitive operation. The e2e tests verify that only admins should be able to create invites (returning 403 for regular members), but this permission check is too permissive. This security issue allows unauthorized users to generate invite tokens that could be used to add members to teams without proper authorization.

issues.title: Inverted logic causes wrong invite URLs for organizations vs teams
issues.description: The condition `if (isOrgContext)` returns the team invite link format when it should return the organization signup format, and vice versa. Organization invites need to direct users to the signup flow with callback to getting-started, but will incorrectly receive the teams URL. Regular team invites need the teams URL but will incorrectly receive the signup URL with callback. This breaks the entire invite flow by sending users to the wrong destination based on whether they're joining an organization or a regular team.

issues.title: Wrong token value returned breaks invite link functionality
issues.description: The method returns `newToken.identifier` which contains the database identifier string 'invite-link-for-teamId-{teamId}' instead of returning the actual random hex token that was generated. This means the invite link will embed this identifier string in the URL instead of the actual verification token. When users attempt to use the invite link, the token lookup will fail because the identifier is not a valid token value, completely breaking the invite acceptance flow.

issues.title: Service filename does not match PascalCase class name
issues.description: Rule requires service filenames to match the exported class name exactly in PascalCase (e.g., TeamService.ts). This service class is `TeamService` but the file is named `teamService.ts` (camelCase), violating the naming convention.
issues.rule_name: Repository and Service Classes Must Follow Naming Conventions

pr.title: Code Review Bench PR #26644 - feat: api v2 team invite link endpoint

structured_output.summary:
This PR adds `POST /v2/teams/:teamId/invite`: a new `TeamsInviteController` and module, output DTOs, and wiring into `PlatformEndpointsModule`. It reuses `TeamService.createInvite`. The NestJS scaffolding follows existing conventions, but the change has three serious bugs. Two of them are in the shared `TeamService`, so they affect the existing web app too.

First, the endpoint is guarded with `@Roles("TEAM_MEMBER")` even though the description, the docs and the e2e tests all say `TEAM_ADMIN`, so any team member can create invite links. Second, `createInvite` now returns the verification token's `identifier` (`invite-link-for-teamId-<id>`) instead of the secret token. Third, the `isOrgContext` check in `buildInviteLink` was flipped, so org and regular-team links point to the wrong flows. The tRPC `createInvite` handler that powers the web UI calls the same service, so the token and link bugs break existing invite links there as well. The new e2e tests would fail against this code (the non-admin 403 check and the `inviteLink` contains `token` check).
structured_output.verdictRationale: I'm requesting changes because of three blocking bugs: the endpoint lets plain members create invites when it should require an admin, the service returns the wrong token, and the org/team link routing is inverted. The last two also break the existing web app's invite flow.

architecture.overview:
API v2 team endpoints are NestJS controllers under `apps/api/v2/src/modules/teams/*`. Each one is protected by `ApiAuthGuard`, which authenticates the caller, and `RolesGuard`, which reads the `:teamId` route param and the `@Roles` metadata, then checks the caller's membership through `MembershipsRepository` with Redis caching. Business logic for invite links already lives in `TeamService.createInvite` in `@calcom/features`, which the tRPC `viewer.teams.createInvite` handler also uses.

The PR adds a thin `TeamsInviteController` in a new `TeamsInviteModule`, registered in `PlatformEndpointsModule`. The controller delegates directly to the static `TeamService.createInvite(teamId)` and wraps the result in `{status, data}`. The PR also edits `TeamService` itself: it changes which field is returned as `token` and flips the branch condition in `buildInviteLink`. Both edits change behavior for every existing caller, not only the new endpoint.
steps: `PlatformEndpointsModule` now imports `TeamsInviteModule`, which provides the controller and imports `PrismaModule`, `RedisModule` and `MembershipsModule` so `RolesGuard` can be resolved.
`TeamsInviteController.createInvite` handles `POST /v2/teams/:teamId/invite`, guarded by `ApiAuthGuard` and `RolesGuard` with the `@Roles` level set on the handler.
The controller calls `TeamService.createInvite(teamId)`, which looks up the team, creates a `verificationToken` row and builds the link.
`buildInviteLink` picks either `/teams?token=` or `/signup?token=&callbackUrl=` depending on whether the team is an org or belongs to one.
The shared `TeamService` is also called by `packages/trpc/.../createInvite.handler.ts`, so its changes reach the web UI too.

findings.title: Endpoint requires only TEAM_MEMBER, so any member can create invite links
findings.fixPrompt: In `apps/api/v2/src/modules/teams/invite/controllers/teams-invite.controller.ts` line 33, the `createInvite` handler uses `@Roles("TEAM_MEMBER")`, so non-admin members can create invite links. Change it to `@Roles("TEAM_ADMIN")` to match the other mutating team endpoints (e.g. `teams-memberships.controller.ts`) and the e2e test expecting 403 for members.

findings.title: createInvite returns the token identifier instead of the secret token
findings.fixPrompt: In `packages/features/ee/teams/services/teamService.ts` `createInvite` (around lines 88-100), the returned `token` is `newToken.identifier` (the constant `invite-link-for-teamId-<id>`) instead of the generated random token. Return the generated `token` (or `newToken.token`) so it matches the token embedded in `inviteLink`. The unused `newToken` variable can be removed. This service is also used by `packages/trpc/server/routers/viewer/teams/createInvite.handler.ts`.

findings.title: Inverted org-context check in buildInviteLink swaps org and team invite URLs
findings.fixPrompt: In `packages/features/ee/teams/services/teamService.ts` `buildInviteLink` (line 106), the condition was inverted to `if (isOrgContext)`, so org/org-sub-team invites get the `/teams?token=` link and regular teams get the `/signup` link. Restore `if (!isOrgContext)` so non-org teams return the `/teams?token=` link and org contexts use `/signup?token=...&callbackUrl=<gettingStartedPath>`. Consider adding unit tests in `teamService.test.ts` covering both branches of `createInvite`.

findings.title: No unit coverage for createInvite; e2e tests only cover regular teams
findings.fixPrompt: Add unit tests in `packages/features/ee/teams/services/teamService.test.ts` for `TeamService.createInvite`: (1) regular team returns `${WEBAPP_URL}/teams?token=<token>`; (2) org or team with parentId returns `/signup?token=<token>&callbackUrl=...`; (3) returned `token` equals the token passed to `prisma.verificationToken.create`. In `apps/api/v2/src/modules/teams/invite/controllers/teams-invite.controller.e2e-spec.ts`, assert on the link path for the regular team and add an org sub-team case.

findings.title: Unused GetUser import and unrelated EOF newline removal
findings.fixPrompt: Remove the unused `GetUser` import from `apps/api/v2/src/modules/teams/invite/controllers/teams-invite.controller.ts` (line 3), and restore the trailing newline at the end of `packages/features/ee/teams/services/teamService.ts`.

findings.title: Good reuse of existing service and module conventions
findings.body: The controller is a thin wrapper over `TeamService.createInvite` rather than duplicating the token and link logic. The module imports exactly what `RolesGuard` needs (`MembershipsModule`, `RedisModule`), matching ::file{file="apps/api/v2/src/modules/teams/memberships/teams-memberships.module.ts"}. The output DTOs follow the standard `{status, data}` envelope with Swagger annotations, and the e2e tests cover the admin, member and non-member cases.
